**Refined prompt:** Answer whether two articles created with identical titles end up with the same slug in this TypeORM RealWorld API — reading the actual slug-generation and slug-consumption code rather than assuming — and say what the system does (or fails to do) if a collision ever happens. Answer as a code-grounded explanation with file:line citations, not a change.

**No — different slugs.** `slugify()` appends randomness, so the title is only the prefix:

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts:201-203
slugify(title: string) {
  return slug(title, {lower: true}) + '-' + (Math.random() * Math.pow(36, 6) | 0).toString(36)
}
```

Two `"How to Train Your Dragon"` articles become `how-to-train-your-dragon-w3f2ql` and `how-to-train-your-dragon-8k1x0p`. Keyspace is ~2.18×10⁹, so even 10,000 same-title articles collide with probability ~2×10⁻⁵ (birthday bound).

But "unlikely" is doing all the work here, because **nothing enforces it**:

- The column is a plain `@Column()` — no unique index (`src/article/article.entity.ts:11-12`, confirmed in `.claude/knowledge/schema.md:31`).
- `create()` slugifies and saves in one shot with no pre-check for an existing slug (`src/article/article.service.ts:175-179`).

So the DB will happily accept a duplicate. And if one ever lands, the read/write paths degrade badly:

- Every lookup is `findOne({slug})` (`article.service.ts:97`, `:102`, `:132`, `:148`, `:166`) → returns an arbitrary one of the two rows.
- `delete()` is `this.articleRepository.delete({ slug: slug })` (`article.service.ts:198`) — that compiles to `DELETE FROM article WHERE slug = ?`, which removes **every** matching row. One user deleting their article would take the other person's with it.

## The collision that isn't random at all

The random suffix protects against accidental collisions. It does nothing about deliberate ones, because `update()` merges the raw body onto the entity:

```ts
// src/article/article.service.ts:190-195
let toUpdate = await this.articleRepository.findOne({ slug: slug});
let updated = Object.assign(toUpdate, articleData);
```

`PUT /api/articles/:slug` has no validation pipe, so `{"article": {"slug": "how-to-train-your-dragon-w3f2ql"}}` writes that slug verbatim onto a different row — an exact collision, on demand. This is LESSONS.md #112. Worse, `@Put(':slug')` (`article.controller.ts:59-63`) has no ownership check despite its `403 Forbidden` annotation at `:58`, so any authenticated user can point their article's slug at yours (LESSONS.md #6/#44; both items are open in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:10-12`).

## One real bug in the suffix itself

`| 0` is a ToInt32 coercion, but 36⁶ = 2,176,782,336 exceeds 2³¹−1 = 2,147,483,647. Draws in the top 29,298,688 values (**~1.35%**) wrap negative, and `(-1987654321).toString(36)` keeps the sign — so roughly one article in 74 gets a slug like `my-title--x9kq2f` with a double hyphen. Also, leading zeros are dropped by `toString(36)`, so the suffix is 1–6 chars, not the 6 the expression implies. Neither reduces uniqueness meaningfully (negative-prefixed strings are still distinct), but the double-dash is user-visible in URLs. *(Arithmetic, not executed — the node one-liner needed approval I didn't have.)*

## Scope

I read `article.service.ts`, `article.entity.ts`, `article.controller.ts`, and the KB's `schema.md`/`workspace.md`. I did **not** check the `slug` npm package's internals (`^1.1.0`, `package.json:44`), so I'm not asserting what it returns for a title with no transliterable ASCII — if it returns `''`, the slug would be bare-suffix-only, which is worth a test. I also skipped `prisma/`, which `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:23-24` marks as not the production path.
